messages.content: You write dialogue that reveals character through voice and rhythm.
Write a dialogue between a detective and a suspect during interrogation. The detective bluffs about having evidence. The suspect is innocent but acts guilty out of fear.

message.content:
# The Interrogation

---

The fluorescent light buzzed. It had been buzzing for forty minutes.

Detective Marra leaned back in her chair, the leather creaking like a warning. She let the silence stretch, watching the man across the table pick at a hangnail until it bled.

"Michael," she said, finally. "Michael, Michael, Michael."

He flinched. "I already told you everything. I told the uniform everything when they—"

"You told them what you *thought* mattered." She slid a folder across the table without opening it. "We're not always real clear on what matters until we know more."

Michael's eyes dropped to the folder. His jaw worked. "What's that?"

"Evidence." She said it like she was reading a grocery list. "We got a lot of it."

"I wasn't—there wasn't—I don't know what you're—"

"Michael." Her voice didn't rise. That was the trick. Never rise. "Take a breath."

He breathed. It sounded like a leak.

"I know you were at the Whitmore residence on the night of the fourteenth," she said. "Between nine and eleven."

"I was just—" He stopped. Swallowed. "Okay. Okay, yes. I was there. But I wasn't doing anything wrong. I was just—I was bringing back a book I borrowed. From Claire. Claire Whitmore. I borrowed it like two months ago and I finally finished it and I figured I'd return it, you know, before it got to be weird."

Marra said nothing.

"It got to be weird," he said.

"Uh-huh."

"No, I mean—okay, it was weird. I admit it was weird. But I wasn't—I didn't go inside. I just left it on the porch. I knocked, nobody answered, so I left it. That's it. That's the whole thing."

"Funny thing about porches," Marra said. "They have lights. Motion sensors. Yours truly tripped one at 9:47."

Michael's face went the color of old paste. "You have footage of me?"

"We have footage."

"Then why are we even—" He caught himself. His hands had gone to his hair, pulling it back from his forehead in these little frantic tugs. "I mean. Good. That's good. That proves I was just there and left."

"Does it?"

"Does it *what*?"

"Prove that."

Michael's mouth opened. Closed. Opened again. "What else would it prove?"
